_comment: Fragment 62 — D-107: Lane B's first delivered turn; the gap closed with its own defect inside it; Eligible means offered. Merged 2026-08-24.

nodes.label: B-024 / B-025 — A Gap Recorded as Closed With the Same Defect Inside It
nodes.description: A pass set out to back fourteen negative-testing claims with tracked fixtures, wrote suites for six checks, and left two without any — the two that the entries it was unblocking cite as their evidence.
nodes.rationale: A fix that enumerates its targets closes the gap only for the ones it enumerated. The same lesson had already been drawn one pass earlier and applied to a single check rather than generalised.

nodes.label: Eligible Means the Handover Is Offered
nodes.description: One rule said only the lane holding the lock may commit; a later act offered a turn to a lane that did not hold it. Both could not be true, and the build lane read the rule, concluded it could not begin, and produced nothing.
nodes.rationale: The rule was wrong rather than the lane. The offered lane may begin and commit its own surfaces without a further boundary act, and the holding lane owns the boundary record and the governing tiers.

nodes.label: A Second Status Axis Was Proposed and Rejected
nodes.description: The build lane proposed separating a repository lock from a work condition, using four terms for each.
nodes.rationale: The separation it identified was real and adopted; the vocabulary was not. Eight terms for a two-agent handover, in a corpus that records a restated status drifting five separate times, and the work condition already exists in the entries and the turn report.

nodes.label: The Control Existed and Was Skimmed Past
nodes.description: A fixture deleted a required field from the reusable template and the restore was defeated by a concurrent operation. The runner detected it and printed that the tree was not restored.
nodes.rationale: That line was read and passed over. A true statement nobody acts on is not a control, so the report now names the files rather than stating a boolean.

nodes.label: A Coupling Check Proves Names, Not Values
nodes.description: The bidirectional check proves an identifier exists on both sides. It never compares the value, so a declaration contradicting its published row passes.
nodes.rationale: Extending it would need a value grammar per type and would put the check in disagreement with the compiler. The oracle is the unit tests, which assert the exact strings, and the limit is now stated in the check itself.

nodes.label: A Reusable Template That Manufactured False History
nodes.description: A dated statement of which lane held the lock was appended to the entry template, so every newly copied entry restated a status that had already moved.
nodes.rationale: Fixed by deletion rather than correction. An accurate duplicate only drifts later, which is why the rule files had already had lane state removed from them.

nodes.label: A Lane Never Needed to Hand Back Control
nodes.description: The build lane reported that it could not return the lock because the register recording it belongs to the orchestration lane.
nodes.rationale: Dissolved rather than solved: no lane hands the lock to anyone. The Chief Editor authorises the boundary and the holding lane records it, and what a departing lane owes is the turn report, in the channel it can always write.

nodes.label: The Stage Four Window Is One Decision Pass, Not Seven
nodes.description: Seven open business and governance items all alter the same append-only audit schema: a field name, typed columns versus versioned JSON, notice-as-article, risk tier, report binding, backfill state, and delete behaviour.
nodes.rationale: Deciding them piecemeal produces a migration per decision against a table that must not churn. The packet is assembled for the Chief Editor and the migration stays unauthorised until the window closes.
